title: Range Mapping Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Pick an input range and an output range, move the input value, and see the linear mapping formula fill in with real numbers, including clamping and int() rounding.

learningObjectives: Apply out_min + (x - in_min) / (in_max - in_min) * (out_max - out_min) to predict a mapped value.
Choose input and output ranges for a robot task such as servo angle to duty or distance to bar height.
Predict how clamping and int() truncation change a mapped value.
prerequisites: Servo angle range and duty values (Chapter 7)

controls.label: Preset
controls.purpose: Load a robot example or unlock the range boxes.

controls.label: in_min, in_max, out_min, out_max
controls.purpose: The two ranges. Editable only in Custom mode.

controls.label: Clamp output
controls.purpose: Limit the result to the output range.

controls.label: Round to integer
controls.purpose: Drop the decimal part, like Python's int().

limitations: An input range of zero width cannot be mapped; the sim shows a warning instead.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then check with a live worked formula
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter exploration with presets, editable ranges, and a filled-in formula
keyQuestions: What fraction of the input range is x, and where is that same fraction in the output range?
What happens to the result when x is outside the input range?
Why might robot code clamp a mapped value?
commonMisconceptions: A mapped value always lands inside the output range.
int() rounds to the nearest whole number.
An output range must go from small to large.
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the duty value for 45 degrees before moving the slider.
Find the ToF bar height for 150 cm and for 250 cm with and without clamping.
Design a custom mapping for a new sensor-to-actuator task.
